Sunday morning broke with a soft, golden mist clinging to the rolling lawns of the Sterling estate. Inside the master study, the fire in the small marble hearth crackled quietly. Julian sat in an armchair by the window, reading a historical biography, while Clara curled up on the adjacent sofa with a sketchbook, drafting landscape designs for the estate’s summer courtyard renovation.

The heavy oak door opened softly, and the old housekeeper entered carrying a silver tray with fresh coffee and pastries.

"Good morning, Mr. and Mrs. Sterling," she said warmly, setting the tray on the mahogany coffee table. "The morning post has arrived."

"Thank you, Martha," Clara smiled, setting her sketchbook aside.

Julian glanced at the small stack of mail resting on the silver tray. On top was a heavy, cream-colored envelope bearing the official seal of the global innovation council. He picked it up, slicing open the flap with a silver letter opener.

Clara watched him closely, noticing the subtle shift in his expression. "What is it?"

Julian read the letter twice before lowering it to his lap. A slow, satisfied smile spread across his face. "The council has officially ratified Project Sovereign as the global benchmark for decentralized economic infrastructure. They want me to keynote the international summit in Geneva next month."

Clara’s eyes lit up with pride. She stood up, walking over to his chair and wrapping her arms around his neck. "Julian, that’s incredible! You’ve changed the entire landscape of international finance."

"We changed it," Julian corrected gently, taking her hand and kissing her knuckles. "I couldn't have built the foundation without you holding the blueprints."

She laughed softly, leaning down to kiss him. "Well, Geneva sounds lovely. But right now, we have a courtyard garden to plan, and you promised to help me plant the heirloom tomatoes before lunch."

Julian stood up immediately, tossing the letter onto the desk without a second thought. "Heirloom tomatoes over international summits any day of the week."
